code_actions.rationale: Treating-provider documentation (admission H&P, procedure note, discharge summary) documents an acute anterior STEMI (anterior leads V1-V4 and procedure indication 'Acute anterior STEMI'), not an inferior-wall STEMI; principal diagnosis should be recoded to the appropriate anterior I21.0x code.
Discharge summary documents a superficial sternal wound infection (MSSA) arising post-operatively and treated in-hospital; POA should be N (not present on admission).

evidence.quote: A pre-hospital 12-lead ECG demonstrated ST-segment elevation in leads V1-V4 with reciprocal changes, and STEMI activation was called.

Reason for Admission: Acute anterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction with cardiogenic shock requiring primary PCI, mechanical circulatory support, and emergency coronary artery bypass grafting.

policy_citations.section: Validation Criteria › Medical — Cardiogenic Shock without Cardiac Procedure Pathway
policy_citations.quote: [1] Presumption rule: When the medical record documents initiation of mechanical circulatory support (intra-aortic balloon pump, Impella device, or venoarterial ECMO) with provider attribution to hemodynamic instability from cardiac cause, Criterion 2 is presumed satisfied even if the blood pressure thresholds are not explicitly documented as sustained below 90 mmHg, provided the provider documents cardiogenic shock as the indication for device placement.

policy_citations.document: Policy Documents/DRG/Acute Respiratory Failure with Hypoxia.docx
policy_citations.quote: [1] Presumption rule: When the provider documents initiation of invasive mechanical ventilation and attributes the need for ventilation to acute respiratory failure, Criterion 2 (objective hypoxemia measurement) is presumed satisfied even if a pre-intubation room-air ABG is not documented.

system_note: What was billed: principal diagnosis I21.19 (STEMI involving other coronary artery of inferior wall) plus multiple MCC/CC conditions and CABG procedure codes. What the record documents: multiple, concordant clinician notes (admission H&P, interventional cardiology procedure note, discharge/transfer summary) document an acute anterior STEMI (anterior wall), not an inferior-wall STEMI, and describe emergency primary PCI to the proximal LAD followed by emergency 3-vessel CABG (LIMA->LAD, SVG->OM1, SVG->RCA). Key discrepant facts: (1) I21.19 (inferior-wall STEMI) is inconsistent with the contemporaneous provider documentation that repeatedly names 'acute anterior STEMI' (History & Physical p.158; Procedure Note - Emergent Coronary Angiography with Primary PCI p.836; Discharge / Transfer Summary p.1008). Evidence: NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_02.pdf-n9 [p.158] A pre-hospital 12-lead ECG demonstrated ST-segment elevation in leads V1-V4 with reciprocal changes, and STEMI activation was called., NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_02.pdf-n16 Procedure Note - Emergent Coronary Angiography with Primary PCI Indication for Procedure: Acute anterior STEMI with cardiogenic shock, and NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_02.pdf-n860 [p.1008] Reason for Admission: Acute anterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction with cardiogenic shock requiring primary PCI, mechanical circulatory support, and emergency coronary artery bypass grafting. Because the principal diagnosis billed (I21.19) conflicts with repeated treating-provider documentation of anterior-wall STEMI, the principal diagnosis is miscoded/sequenced incorrectly and must be recoded to I21.09 (ST elevation myocardial infarction involving other coronary artery of anterior wall). (2) Cardiogenic shock (R57.0, MCC), cardiac arrest (I46.9, MCC), and acute respiratory failure with hypoxia (J96.01, MCC) are supported: the record documents hemodynamic collapse with Impella CP and IABP placement, vasopressors/inotropes, a pulseless VT arrest with ROSC after ACLS, and invasive mechanical ventilation. Evidence: NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_02.pdf-n9 (H&P) Cardiogenic shock: Impella CP + IABP support; inotropes (dobutamine); norepinephrine for MAP; NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_02.pdf-n16 Indication for Procedure: Acute anterior STEMI with cardiogenic shock, NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_02.pdf-n860 [p.1008]...pulseless ventricular tachycardia arrest on ICU day 4 with successful ROSC after 8 minutes of ACLS and targeted temperature management; Impella CP and intra-aortic balloon pump were placed for hemodynamic support, and the patient was intubated for pulmonary edema. Policy presumption rules: RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Cardiogenic-Shock.docx-b44 [1] Presumption rule: When the medical record documents initiation of mechanical circulatory support (intra-aortic balloon pump, Impella device, or venoarterial ECMO) with provider attribution to hemodynamic instability from cardiac cause, Criterion 2 is presumed satisfied..., and RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Acute-Respiratory-Failure-with-Hypoxia.docx-b37 [1] Presumption rule: When the provider documents initiation of invasive mechanical ventilation and attributes the need for ventilation to acute respiratory failure, Criterion 2 (objective hypoxemia measurement) is presumed satisfied.... These policy rules support keeping R57.0 and J96.01 and I46.9 as billed (MCCs) because the record documents device placement, vasopressors/inotropes, intubation/ventilation and a documented pulseless arrest with ROSC. (3) Acute kidney injury N17.9 (CC) is supported by nephrology consultation documenting contrast-induced KDIGO stage 2 AKI with creatinine peak ~2.8 and oliguria (Nephrology Consultation p.108). Evidence: NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_02.pdf-n30 Nephrology Consultation KDIGO stage 2 AKI from iodinated contrast exposure in setting of cardiogenic shock and poor perfusion. Creatinine peak 2.8; oliguric with adequate response to careful diuresis. (4) Post-operative sternal wound infection (MSSA) and MSSA organism coding: the Discharge/Transfer Summary documents a superficial sternal wound infection with MSSA treated with cefazolin and wound VAC. This is clearly a postoperative infection; the billed procedural-complication/infection T81.4XXA was flagged POA=Y on the claim but the record shows this developed after surgery and therefore POA should be N (hospital-acquired). Evidence: NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_02.pdf-n860 [p.1008] Discharge / Transfer Diagnoses... superficial sternal wound infection (MSSA) on cefazolin with wound VAC; and NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_02.pdf-n860 [p.1008] The post-operative course was complicated by... a superficial sternal wound infection with methicillin-susceptible S. aureus treated with cefazolin and wound VAC therapy. Change of POA is required for T81.4XXA (POA Y->N). (5) Right popliteal DVT (I82.401), postoperative atrial fibrillation (I48.91, POA=N), MSSA organism code (B95.61) and other comorbidities (I50.23, E11.65, I10, E78.5, Z66) are supported by the chart and may remain on the claim; see evidence citations below. (6) Procedure coding: operative documentation describes an emergency 3-vessel CABG with LIMA->LAD and two vein grafts to OM1 and RCA (Procedure Note p.189; Discharge Summary p.1008). The billed PCS list includes 021009W (bypass one site) and 021109W (bypass two sites) as separate lines rather than a single 3-vessel CABG code. There is a documented conflict between the procedure note and the billed bypass-site codes; the record does not allow the auditor engine to definitively determine whether the two billed bypass codes appropriately represent a 3-vessel procedure or whether a single three-site bypass code should have been reported. Human coder review is required to reconcile ICD-10-PCS selection for the CABG (see hitl_question). Evidence: NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_02.pdf-n36 [p.231] Assessment... plan for emergency 3-vessel CABG with LIMA-LAD and vein grafts; NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_02.pdf-n860 [p.1008] emergency 3-vessel coronary artery bypass grafting (LIMA to LAD, SVG to OM1 and RCA). Audit action summary: Recode principal diagnosis from the billed I21.19 (inferior-wall STEMI) to I21.09 (ST elevation myocardial infarction involving other coronary artery of anterior wall) to reflect treating-provider documentation; change POA for the infection T81.4XXA from Y to N; keep cardiogenic shock (R57.0), cardiac arrest (I46.9), acute respiratory failure (J96.01), AKI (N17.9), I48.91 (post-operative AF) and other comorbidities as supported. Leave procedure list as billed for now but escalate for human review to reconcile CABG-site PCS coding to the operative report. Citations: NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_02.pdf-n9 (History & Physical, p.158), NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_02.pdf-n16 (Procedure Note - Emergent Coronary Angiography with Primary PCI, p.836), NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_02.pdf-n36 (Cardiothoracic Surgery Consultation, p.231), NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_02.pdf-n30 (Nephrology Consultation, p.108), NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_02.pdf-n860 (Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.1008), RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Cardiogenic-Shock.docx-b44 (presumption rule for MCS), RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Acute-Respiratory-Failure-with-Hypoxia.docx-b37 (presumption rule for mechanical ventilation).
rationale_letter: Dear Provider, We audited the inpatient DRG coding for claim MR_02 (admission 2026-01-17). Our review compared what was billed to the documentation in the medical record and to the payer’s DRG coding validation policies. The audit found the following: Finding: Principal diagnosis miscoded and POA error for post-operative wound infection. Basis: The treating clinicians consistently documented an acute anterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction as the index event (History & Physical, Procedure Note, Discharge Summary). Example documentation includes: a pre-hospital 12-lead ECG with ST-elevation in leads V1–V4 and the interventional cardiology procedure indication listed as 'Acute anterior STEMI with cardiogenic shock' (History & Physical p.158; Procedure Note p.836). The discharge/transfer summary likewise lists 'Acute anterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction with cardiogenic shock requiring primary PCI... and emergency 3-vessel CABG' (Discharge / Transfer Summary p.1008). The claim was billed with I21.19 (STEMI involving other coronary artery of inferior wall) in principal position; the documentation consistently supports anterior-wall STEMI and therefore should be recoded to I21.09. In addition, the record documents a postoperative superficial sternal wound infection due to methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus treated with cefazolin and wound VAC; this is described in the post-operative course and discharge summary as a complication of the operative course, so the procedure-related infection code (T81.4XXA) should be flagged POA = N (hospital-acquired), not POA = Y as billed (Discharge / Transfer Summary p.1008). Supported findings: cardiogenic shock (R57.0), cardiac arrest with ROSC (I46.9), and acute respiratory failure with hypoxia (J96.01) are supported by the chart (device placement Impella/IABP, vasopressors/inotropes, documented pulseless VT with ROSC, intubation/mechanical ventilation) and meet policy validation criteria (see Policy: Cardiogenic Shock presumption for mechanical circulatory support and Acute Respiratory Failure presumption for invasive ventilation). Correction being made: Principal diagnosis I21.19 will be changed to I21.09 (per chart documentation). The POA indicator for T81.4XXA (infection following a procedure) will be changed from Y to N. The remainder of the diagnosis codes (R57.0, J96.01, I46.9, N17.9, I48.91, I82.401, B95.61, chronic comorbidities) are supported and will be retained. Next steps / request: Please provide any additional documentation that specifies the anatomic STEMI code (if provider-specified code differs from the chart narrative) or clarifies if the sternal wound infection was present on admission. Also please confirm operative/procedure-code selection for the CABG (operative report documents an emergency 3-vessel CABG) so we can confirm the correct ICD-10-PCS code(s). If no additional documentation is available, we will finalize the corrections as above and adjust claim coding accordingly. Sincerely, Clinical Claims Audit Team
